transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hi, yeah, thanks for fitting me in. It's... well, to be honest, the main thing, the thing that really actually scared me into finally making an appointment and coming in today, is my eating. It's just been completely all over the place lately, and I mean completely. 

Like, I'm out on the road a lot for work—I do wholesale and manufacturing sales, so I'm always driving from client to client, pitching products, checking on accounts, that whole thing—and lately, some days I just forget meals completely. Like, I'll look at the dashboard clock and it's 7 PM and I haven't had a single bite of food all day, not even a protein bar from a gas station, and I don't even feel hungry. It just doesn't cross my mind at all. 

But then, on the flip side, other nights I'm just tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight. I'll order a massive amount of Chinese food or pizza, eat all of that, and then I'm still rummaging through the kitchen for chips, crackers, whatever I can get my hands on at 2 AM. It's like a switch flips and I just can't stop stuffing my face, but then the very next day I'm back to literally eating nothing without even meaning to. It's really freaking me out, honestly, because I've usually been pretty regular about grabbing lunch between sales calls or having a normal dinner, but now it's just this extreme back and forth and I don't know what's going on with my body.
Do you usually feel guilty after those late-night eating episodes?

Well, yeah, I mean, sure, I feel bad about the food, like, physically bad, and maybe a little stupid for eating an entire large pepperoni pizza and a mountain of crab rangoon by myself at 2 AM. But honestly, the food guilt is just a drop in the bucket compared to the other stuff going on in my head when I'm sitting there surrounded by all those empty takeout boxes. 

That's when the real guilt hits, you know? Because my mind just starts racing and I can't shut it off. It's work. It's always work. I just... I keep replaying every single mistake I made with those Providence accounts. I don't know if you know anything about wholesale, but Providence was supposed to be this huge break for me, like, a total game-changer for my quarter and my commission. I had the meetings set up, I had the product samples, and I just completely messed it up. 

So I'll be sitting there in the middle of the night, and I just keep going over every email I sent, every phone call, every little thing I said wrong or forgot to follow up on, just beating myself up over it. And I just sit there thinking I blew my whole future. Like, my entire career in sales is just done because I can't even handle a basic account expansion. I just feel so completely useless. And the worst part, the absolute worst part, is I know everybody at work can see it. I walk into the regional office and I swear my manager and the other reps are just looking at me like I'm a total fraud, like they all know I dropped the ball and I'm just taking up space. It's just this heavy, crushing feeling that I'm totally worthless, and it just loops in my head over and over and over while I'm eating, and I just can't make it stop.
Do you usually start eating late at night as a way to try and stop thinking about work and those feelings of guilt and worthlessness?

Well, I don't know if I'd say I start eating specifically *to* stop thinking about it. It's not like a conscious plan, you know? It's not like I'm sitting there going, "Man, I feel terrible about that Providence account, let me go eat an entire pizza so I can just turn my brain off for a few hours." It's really not like that at all. 

It's more like... I'll just be up late, pacing around the apartment or sitting on the edge of the couch, and my brain is just hammering me with all those emails and the missed calls and the way my manager looked at me in the hallway. And then suddenly, I'm just in the kitchen. I don't even really remember making the decision to go in there. I'll just find myself standing there in the dark with the refrigerator door open, the little bulb shining on me, and I'm just grabbing whatever is in front of my face. A block of cheese, some leftover rice, a half-empty box of stale crackers. And then I'll pull out my phone and order the takeout. 

So I don't think I'm doing it to push the thoughts away, because honestly, the thoughts don't even stop when I'm eating! That's the crazy part. I'll be three or four slices deep into a pepperoni pizza, just chewing mechanically, and I'm still right there in my head, agonizing over that quarterly projection spreadsheet I messed up or rehearsing what I should have said to the purchasing director. If the food is supposed to be some kind of distraction, it's a really, really bad one, because the guilt and that heavy feeling are just sitting right there at the kitchen counter with me the entire time. It's just this endless loop. I don't know, maybe my body is just completely confused because I forgot to eat while I was out driving between clients all day, but my brain definitely isn't taking a break while I'm stuffing my face, that's for sure. It just keeps running and running.
Do you think the eating helps you feel better emotionally at all, even if it's just for a moment?

No... no, not really. I mean, you'd think it would, right? Like, you always see people on TV eating a whole pint of ice cream or whatever when they're upset because it's supposed to be comfort food. But honestly? There is zero comfort in it for me. None at all. It doesn't make me feel better, not even for a split second. 

It's more like... it's just this mechanical thing my body is doing. Like I was saying with the Chinese food the other night, I'm sitting there on my couch, dipping a crab rangoon into the sweet and sour sauce, taking a bite, chewing, swallowing, and I'm not thinking, "Oh man, this tastes so good, I feel so much better." I'm not feeling any kind of relief. I'm just chewing while my brain is still going a million miles an hour, still screaming at me about my commission and the Providence account and how I'm probably going to get fired. 

If anything, it honestly just makes me feel worse, because then you add the physical grossness on top of the mental stuff. So I'm sitting there, my brain is telling me I'm a total failure and a fraud, and now my stomach is stretched out and hurting because I just shoved three thousand calories of grease into it at 3 AM for absolutely no reason. So, yeah, no emotional boost whatsoever. I don't even really taste the food half the time. It's just my jaw moving while everything else is crashing down around me. It really doesn't help at all.
Have you lost any weight recently?

Well, honestly, that's... that's kind of the main thing that finally scared me enough to actually make this appointment and come in to see you. Because my weight and my eating habits have just been completely, totally all over the place lately, and I don't really understand what's happening with my body. 

Like, it's not a steady thing where I'm just gaining or losing consistently. It's this wild pendulum swing. Some days, especially when I'm out on the road, driving from client to client, trying to fix the mess I made with the Providence account, I'll just completely forget to eat. Like, an entire day will go by, and it'll be 7 PM, and I'll realize the only thing I've had is three black coffees and a stick of gum. I just don't even feel hungry. My stomach doesn't growl, nothing. I'm just so wired and stressed out that food doesn't even cross my mind. 

But then, you know, like I was just saying, other nights it's the exact opposite extreme. It'll be past midnight, and suddenly I'm just tearing through whatever I can find. I'm ordering that pizza, or the Chinese takeout, and I'm just inhaling it, plus whatever snacks I have in the pantry, just eating until I physically can't anymore. So my body is just getting yanked back and forth between practically starving and then getting overloaded with thousands of calories at 2 AM. 

And because of that, my weight is just fluctuating all over the map. I'll drop a few pounds when I have a string of those days where I forget to eat, my pants will feel a little looser, and then I'll have a few nights of the crazy midnight binging, and suddenly I feel bloated and heavy again. It's just so erratic. I don't feel in control of it at all, and it really freaked me out enough to realize I needed to talk to somebody about what's going on with me.
Do you ever eat in response to feelings other than guilt, such as anxiety or sadness?

I mean, sadness? I don't really think I'm sitting around crying and eating, if that's what you mean. Anxiety, sure, I guess, because I'm constantly stressed about my numbers and my accounts and trying to keep my head above water at work. But... well, honestly, like I was just trying to explain a second ago, I don't even know if I can tie it to one specific feeling like that, because the whole pattern is just completely broken right now. 

Honestly, that exact thing is what scared me into coming in here to see you in the first place. My eating has just been so completely all over the place that I can't even make sense of it anymore. It's not a simple cause-and-effect thing where I'm like, "Oh, I feel anxious right now, let me go have a snack." It's so much more extreme than that. Like I said, it's this massive swing. Some days I'm so wound up and stressed about my route that I just forget meals completely. I'll be out on the road, hitting up different warehouses, talking to clients, and I just won't eat a single thing all day. My brain doesn't even register that I need food. 

And then, out of nowhere, it's the total opposite. Other nights I'm just tearing through takeout and whatever random snacks I can find in my cupboards way past midnight, just eating until I feel sick. So whether it's anxiety or guilt or whatever is going on in my head, it just feels like my body doesn't know how to eat normally right now. It's just this huge, terrifying swing back and forth between nothing at all and a total binge, and not having any control over that is really what pushed me to finally make the call to come in today. I just can't keep living with it being this erratic.
Do you think your eating habits are related to trying to cope with your emotional distress?

Well, I mean... I don't know if "coping" is the right word, honestly. Because, like I've been saying, it doesn't actually help. It doesn't make the distress go away or even quiet it down for a second. If I was coping, wouldn't I feel at least a little bit better? But I don't. 

But I guess... I mean, maybe on some subconscious level, my brain is just short-circuiting because of all the stress and the guilt and the anxiety about work and everything else. But honestly, the whole thing is just so confusing to me. It's not like I'm sitting there thinking, "I feel bad, I should eat to feel better." It's more like my body has just completely forgotten how to function normally. 

And like I keep saying, because I know I sound like a broken record here, but honestly, the thing that scared me into coming in is that my eating has just been all over the place. It's completely erratic. It's like I have no middle ground anymore. Some days, I'm so wrapped up in my head, driving around, stressing about my route and my numbers, that I just forget meals completely. Like, a whole day will go by, and I haven't eaten a single thing, and I don't even feel hungry. It's like my stomach is just turned off. 

But then, out of nowhere, it flips. Other nights, I'm just tearing through takeout and whatever snacks I can find in the pantry after midnight. I'm just inhaling food, not even tasting it, just eating until I feel physically sick. And it's that extreme swing—from nothing at all to a massive binge—that really freaked me out. It's not a coping mechanism, it's more like I've just completely lost control of my own body and my own habits. And that's what made me finally pick up the phone and make this appointment, because I just can't keep living with it being this chaotic.
Are your eating habits and the stress from work affecting your relationships with others?

Relationships... yeah. I mean, it's affecting everything. It's not just that I might be a little distant or whatever with people, it's really bleeding into my actual livelihood, which affects my whole life, you know? 

Like, at work, things are just... they're getting really bad. My manager—he's been my manager for a couple of years, usually we're totally fine—he has actually started pulling me off some of my regular accounts. And these are accounts I've built up over time! But I can't even really argue with him about it because, honestly, I'm making these really stupid mistakes that I normally wouldn't ever make. Like, totally messing up order sheets for the manufacturing guys, or just completely blanking on sending the wholesale invoices out on time. My brain is just so fried from all the stress and the weird eating swings that I just can't focus on the details anymore. 

And then... well, it got to the point where I was just so overwhelmed that I actually called that employee-assistance hotline thing we have. I was just sitting in my car between client visits, totally freaking out, and I made the call. But then, because of that, HR somehow got involved. So now I've got human resources breathing down my neck, scheduling these little meetings to check on me, which just adds a whole other massive layer of anxiety to my day. 

I mean, I'm still showing up. I'm still getting out of bed, getting in the car, and driving my route every single day. I'm trying so hard to just push through it and act like I've got it together. But honestly? Between the HR stuff, losing my accounts, and just the total chaos when I get back to my house every night... work and home both just feel like they’re completely slipping out of my control. Like I'm holding onto a rope and it's just burning through my hands, and I don't know how to get a grip on my life anymore.
Are you avoiding social situations because of your eating habits?

Well, I mean... it's not just the eating, honestly. It's not like I'm sitting at home thinking, "Oh, I can't go out because people will see me eat weirdly." It's... it's so much bigger than that. It's like everything just feels incredibly flat right now. I don't know how else to describe it. 

Like, take my weekends, for example. I used to be so active. I played in this recreational soccer league every single Saturday morning. I loved it. I loved the guys on the team, I loved the competition, I loved getting a good sweat in. I haven't been to a game in weeks. I just... I can't even fathom putting on my cleats and running around. It just feels pointless. And it's not just soccer. I used to really enjoy cooking for my girlfriend, you know? Like, actually going to the store, picking out ingredients, spending an hour or two making something really nice for us. Now? The thought of even boiling water just seems exhausting. I just don't care. 

And it's weird stuff, too. Like, I used to love checking out these little small art galleries downtown on Sunday afternoons. Just wandering around, looking at stuff, taking it all in. I haven't done that in forever. I just have zero desire to go. Even at work, which I know I was just talking about being a disaster, but I used to actually like helping the newer sales guys out. Like, showing them the ropes, giving them tips on how to handle difficult clients, maybe grabbing a coffee with them and just talking shop. I was the guy people came to when they had questions. Now, if someone asks me something, I just want to tell them to figure it out themselves. I just... I can't make myself care about any of it anymore. The things that used to make up my life, the things I actually enjoyed doing, they just feel like chores now. So, yeah, I guess I am avoiding social situations, but it's not really about the food. It's just that I don't have the energy or the interest to be around anyone or do anything.
Are there any specific daily activities or relationships that you feel are being affected by your current eating habits?

I mean... specific activities affected *just* by the eating? Not really. I don't think so. Because, like I was just trying to explain, it's not the food itself that's stopping me from doing things. 

I guess, I mean, if you want to get really technical about it, my grocery shopping routine is completely shot, but that's just because I'm either not eating a single thing all day or I'm panic-ordering a massive amount of takeout at one in the morning. But as far as my relationships go? It's not the food causing the rift. Like with my girlfriend... sure, she notices it. She'll come over to my place and see, I don't know, a mountain of empty containers and wrappers in the trash from the night before, and she'll give me this look, you know? It's this very specific, worried, almost pitying look that I just absolutely hate. She asks if I'm eating okay, and I just kind of brush it off. But we aren't actually fighting about the food. It's not like my eating habits are the thing ruining our relationship directly, it's just the fact that I have zero energy to actually be a good boyfriend right now. 

And with work... well, I already told you about the HR nightmare and my manager pulling my accounts. The crazy eating swings definitely make my brain feel like absolute mush the next day, which makes the job so much harder, but it's not like I'm bingeing *during* a client meeting or something. I'm doing all of that completely alone, at night, in my own house, when nobody is around to see it. It's a very isolated thing. Nobody actually watches me do it. 

So, no, I don't think there are specific relationships or daily things being ruined *just* because I'm starving myself all day and then eating everything in sight at midnight. It's more just the general exhaustion and the brain fog from all of it that's bleeding into my life. I just really want to be clear about that, because I'm not, like, hiding in the bathroom to eat during a date, or blowing off my buddies just so I can stay home and order food. It's just the aftermath of the whole chaotic cycle that gets me, not the eating itself. Does that make sense? Because I feel like I'm talking in circles, but they really are two different things in my head.
Are you feeling like your eating habits are affecting your ability to perform your job or maintain relationships with your loved ones?

I mean, like I was saying before, the eating stuff isn't the direct cause, but... yeah, I guess it's all connected, right? Because I'm not eating all day and then I'm just gorging myself at night, I'm waking up feeling completely trashed. And that's definitely affecting my job. I mean, I'm making these really dumb mistakes on order sheets and wholesale invoices that I never used to make. It's embarrassing, honestly. 

And my manager—who I usually get along with great, we've always had a solid working relationship—he's noticed. He's actually started pulling me off some of my regular accounts. These are clients I've spent months, sometimes years, building trust with, and now I'm just losing them because I can't keep my head straight. And then there's the whole HR thing. Because I was just so stressed and overwhelmed, I called that employee-assistance hotline from my car one day, and somehow that triggered HR getting involved. So now I have them breathing down my neck, scheduling these little check-in meetings that just make me feel like I'm under a microscope all day. 

So, yeah, I'm still showing up. I get up every morning, I get in my car, and I drive my route. I'm trying to hold it together. But honestly? Between losing my accounts, the HR meetings, and just the absolute mess my head is in... it feels like both work and my home life are completely slipping out of my control. It's like I'm trying to hold onto a handful of sand and it's just slipping right through my fingers, and I don't know how to stop it.
Do you feel like you're hiding your eating habits from others due to feelings of guilt or shame?

Well, I mean... I guess there's a little bit of shame with the food, like I mentioned with my girlfriend seeing all the trash and giving me that pitying look. But honestly? When we talk about guilt or feeling ashamed, the eating stuff is barely a blip on my radar compared to everything else. The real guilt, the stuff that actually makes my chest physically ache and keeps me staring at the ceiling for hours, is work. 

It's... I just keep replaying every single mistake I made with those Providence accounts. Over and over and over, like a movie I can't turn off. I'll be driving or trying to watch TV, and suddenly I'm just agonizing over a wholesale quote I botched, or an inventory email I completely forgot to send. I spent so much time building trust with those Providence guys, learning their supply chains, doing all the groundwork, and I just wrecked it. I honestly feel like I blew my whole future. Like, my entire career in this industry is just done because of this. I sit there and I just feel so incredibly useless. 

And the absolute worst part is that I know everybody at work can see it. It's not a secret. My manager pulled the accounts, HR is doing their little check-ins, and I know the other reps in the bullpen are watching it all happen. They have to be talking about it. They look at me and they just see this guy who completely dropped the ball and ruined his territory. It's this heavy, suffocating feeling of being a total failure, and it's just so much bigger and deeper than being embarrassed about eating a bunch of takeout at midnight, you know? It's my entire livelihood, my reputation, and everybody can see how useless I am right now. So, yeah, I feel shame, but it's not really about the food. It's about everything else I've ruined.
Do you think your eating habits are a symptom of something else going on with you, or do they seem to be the main problem?

I mean... I don't really know how to answer that, to be perfectly honest with you. It’s like... it’s like trying to untangle a giant knot of fishing line, you know? You pull on one string and it just tightens something else somewhere else. Are the eating habits the main problem? I really, really don't think so. I mean, how could they be? Eating a massive order of takeout at one in the morning isn't what made me mess up the Providence accounts. It’s not what made HR start treating me like some sort of liability. But... is it a symptom of something else? I don't know. I guess maybe? 

It’s just... when I try to sit down and actually think about what’s causing what, my brain just kind of short-circuits. Because on one hand, yeah, obviously I’m stressed out of my mind about work, and when I’m stressed, I forget to eat all day while I'm out driving my route, and then I crash and binge at night. But on the other hand, the not eating and the bingeing makes me feel so physically awful and foggy the next day that I end up making more mistakes at work, which just makes me more stressed. So it’s this endless, exhausting loop. I sit in my car sometimes, just staring at the steering wheel before I go into a client's warehouse, and I try to figure out where it all started going wrong, but it’s all just one big blur of... of failure, honestly. 

So I don't have a good answer for you. I don't know if the food thing is a symptom or a cause or just some weird side effect of my whole life falling apart. It just feels like everything is happening all at once, and I’m just trying to keep my head above water. Separating it out into neat little categories like "main problem" or "symptom" is... it's just really hard for me to do right now. Does that make sense? I just don't know what's driving what anymore.
Are you avoiding any activities or social interactions because you feel guilty or ashamed about your eating habits?

Well, avoiding things... yeah, I am, but again, it's really not about the eating. I mean, I don't care if people see me eat, or know what I eat, that's not the issue at all. The issue is just... I don't know, I just don't have the energy or the desire to do anything anymore. It's like someone just unplugged me from the wall. 

Like, I used to be pretty active. Every weekend, without fail, I'd be out playing in this rec soccer league. I loved it, you know? The running, the competition, just being out on the field with the guys and grabbing a beer after. But the last few months... I just stopped going. I can't even fathom putting on my cleats right now. The thought of running around a field just feels completely pointless. And it's not just soccer. I used to really enjoy cooking, especially for my girlfriend. We'd go to the store, pick out ingredients, and I'd spend a couple of hours making a really nice dinner. Now? I can't even bring myself to boil water. That's why I'm ordering all that takeout in the first place, because the idea of standing in the kitchen and actually preparing something just feels like climbing a mountain. 

And it spills over into other stuff, too. We used to go check out these small art galleries downtown on Sunday afternoons, just walking around, looking at stuff, talking. It was our thing. But now when she asks if I want to go, I just make up some excuse because I'd rather just sit on the couch and stare at the wall. I just don't care about the art, or the walking, or any of it. Even at work, before all this Providence account stuff blew up in my face, I used to actually like helping out the newer sales guys. You know, showing them the ropes, giving them tips on how to handle certain clients, maybe riding along with them for an afternoon. I liked feeling like a mentor, I guess. But now? If one of them asks me a question, I just give them the shortest answer possible so they'll go away. I just... I can't make myself care about their sales numbers or their problems when I feel like I'm drowning in my own. So, yeah, I'm avoiding a lot of things, a lot of interactions, but it's not because I'm hiding a burger wrapper. It's because everything I used to enjoy just feels completely hollow now, and I just don't have the bandwidth to pretend otherwise.
Are there any parts of your daily life or relationships that you feel are being directly affected by your current eating patterns?

Well, I mean... if we're talking about the eating specifically, like the crashing and the brain fog from binging all that takeout and not eating during the day... yeah, it's definitely bleeding into everything. It's all connected, like I was saying before. Because I feel so physically awful and out of it, the mistakes at work have just gotten... they've gotten really bad. 

To the point where my manager—who I’ve always had a pretty solid relationship with, you know, we used to grab beers or go to the driving range sometimes—he’s actually started pulling me off accounts. And not just the Providence ones I was agonizing over earlier, but other ones too, because I'm just making these incredibly stupid, careless mistakes that I normally wouldn't ever make in a million years. Like messing up wholesale delivery dates or quoting the wrong tier pricing to long-term clients. It's humiliating. 

And then... well, then HR got involved. Yeah, they actually stepped in after this whole employee-assistance call happened, which is just a whole other layer of embarrassing on top of everything else. Having human resources sit you down and do their little corporate concern routine, asking all these probing questions... it’s awful. I mean, I’m still showing up every day. I set my alarm, I get in my car, I drive my routes, I go sit in the bullpen. I'm physically there, going through the motions. But honestly? It really just feels like everything—my job, my territory, and even things at home with my girlfriend and the whole dynamic there with me just being a total zombie—it all just feels like it’s completely slipping out of my control. Like I'm gripping the steering wheel as hard as I can, but the car is just sliding on ice anyway, you know? So yeah, the whole cycle with the food and the exhaustion... it's definitely taking a toll on every single part of my day.
Do you think your eating habits are a way to deal with your emotional pain?

Emotional pain... I mean, I guess that’s one way to put it, but I don't know if "pain" is exactly the right word for it. It’s more like this... this crushing, suffocating weight of just knowing how badly I messed everything up. So maybe I am using the food to deal with it, because... well, like I brought up earlier with those Providence accounts? I just can't let it go. My brain won't let me. I keep replaying every single mistake I made with them, over and over and over again. It’s like a terrible movie I can't turn off. 

I’ll be sitting on my couch at two in the morning, surrounded by takeout boxes, just chewing and staring at the wall, and my mind is just running through every missed email, every wrong price tier I quoted to their purchasing manager, every stupid, careless thing I said on those conference calls. And I just sit there thinking that I completely blew my whole future. Like, I had this great territory, I was doing well, I was on track to maybe get promoted to a regional spot in a few years, and I just threw it all in the garbage. It makes me feel so incredibly useless. Just... completely worthless, you know? 

And the absolute worst part about all of it is that I know everybody at work can see it. I walk into the office, or I go sit at my desk in the bullpen, and I can just feel their eyes on me. I know they're looking at me and thinking, "There's the guy who tanked the Providence deal, what a disaster." They all know I'm useless now. Even the new guys I used to train probably think I'm a total joke. So, yeah, maybe when I'm eating, for like ten or fifteen minutes, the physical act of just stuffing my face kind of distracts me from how much of a failure I am. It's like I'm trying to fill up this massive hole of guilt. But it never lasts. As soon as the food is gone, I'm right back to replaying those same exact mistakes and feeling like I have absolutely no future left here.
Do you think your eating habits are directly related to how you're feeling emotionally?

Yeah, I mean, absolutely. There's no way they aren't connected. Because honestly, the emotional part of it... it’s just so heavy, and the eating is just a byproduct of that. Like I was saying about the Providence thing and feeling like a total failure, it’s not just a bad day at the office that you leave behind at five o'clock. It’s this constant, crushing feeling in my chest from the exact minute my alarm goes off in the morning. I hear that buzzing and I just dread opening my eyes. And the food is just... it's just a way to numb out, I guess. It's something to do when I'm sitting there in the dark at night, feeling like my entire life is just slipping through my fingers and I can't stop it. 

But the emotions, they get so bad, and so overwhelming, that lately... well, honestly, I've had these thoughts where I wish I could just not wake up for a while. You know? Like, if I could just go to sleep and stay asleep for a week, or a month, or however long it takes for all this mess to just blow over. Just to get a break from my own brain and all this guilt. Like if I could just hit a pause button on my life so I wouldn't have to deal with HR looking at me with pity, or my manager pulling my accounts, or the disappointment I see on my girlfriend's face when I won't even go to an art gallery with her anymore. I just want to stay asleep so I don't have to feel it. 

I mean, I haven't made a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I want to be clear about that. I'm not sitting here figuring out how to actually do something drastic or, you know, end it all. It’s really not like that. It’s more just this deep, bone-tired exhaustion where the idea of just closing my eyes and not having to wake up and face another day of being a complete failure just sounds like the most peaceful thing in the world right now. So yeah, the takeout, the binging, the hiding on the couch... it’s all just coming from this exact same place of wanting to escape how completely awful I feel inside.
Do you think your eating habits would improve if your work-related stress and emotional issues were resolved?

Would they improve? Man, I... I honestly don't even know how to answer that. I mean, I guess it sounds nice in theory, right? Like, if we could just wave a magic wand and suddenly my manager trusts me again, and HR forgets I ever existed, and the Providence deal is somehow magically back on track... maybe I wouldn't feel the need to sit in the dark and eat three orders of takeout at two in the morning. 

But honestly? I really don't know if fixing the work stuff would just automatically fix the food stuff. Because it’s like... I don't even know what 'resolved' would look like at this point. The stress and the guilt, it's just so deeply baked into who I am right now. Like, even if they gave me all my accounts back tomorrow and told me all is forgiven, I'd still be the guy who messed them up in the first place, you know? My brain would still find a way to torture me about it. 

And the eating... it’s become such a routine now. It’s like this weird, twisted comfort blanket.
